answer.summary: Liu cautions companies that predate GenAI not to mistake adding a few AI features and marketing them as an AI strategy. Instead, he recommends rethinking the mission from a clean slate as if founding an AI-native company, then assessing whether existing assets help or hinder that approach.

sections.heading: The mistake to avoid
sections.content: Liu warns against simply putting “some AI stuff” on the marketing site, adding a couple of AI features, and calling it a day.

sections.heading: What to do instead
sections.content: He recommends a clean-slate test: ask how the company would pursue the same mission if it were being founded now, using a fully AI-native approach. Then evaluate whether the existing product and business provide useful building blocks or whether legacy assets leave the company worse off than starting from scratch. He notes that the answer depends on the product.

judgment.explanation: The answer accurately attributes Liu’s warning against adding a few AI features or marketing changes and calling that sufficient adaptation. It also gives his clean-slate, AI-native reassessment as the alternative, supported by S1.
